title: Gluing the local tower adjunctions
statement:
In the standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], fix a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a smooth separated morphism of finite type, of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$. Use the ordinary derived category of the strict varying-coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers] and its uniformly bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategory [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], with $Rf_{!,\bullet}$ and its finite evaluations as in [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. Tate twists are taken levelwise as in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed].

For each $K_\bullet\in\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$ there is a pair $(G_\bullet,\varepsilon_\bullet(K_\bullet))$, with $G_\bullet=f^!_\bullet K_\bullet\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$ and $\varepsilon_\bullet(K_\bullet):Rf_{!,\bullet}G_\bullet\to K_\bullet$, such that
$$a\longmapsto\varepsilon_\bullet(K_\bullet)\circ Rf_{!,\bullet}(a):\operatorname{Hom}(M_\bullet,G_\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_{!,\bullet}M_\bullet,K_\bullet)$$
is a bijection for every $M_\bullet$ in that category, natural in $M_\bullet$, and:

1. On every coordinate chart $f|_U=p_d\circ e$, $e:U\to\mathbf A^d_Y$ etale, there is a counit-preserving isomorphism $G_\bullet|_U\simeq e_\bullet^*p_{d,\bullet}^*K_\bullet(d)[2d]$. The local counit applies the fibre sum for $e$ followed by iterated projective-line integration.
2. The pair is unique up to unique counit-preserving isomorphism, and $K_\bullet\mapsto f^!_\bullet K_\bullet$ is a functor right adjoint to $Rf_{!,\bullet}$.
3. There are natural isomorphisms $(f^!_\bullet K_\bullet)_n\simeq f^!_{A_n}K_n$, compatible with counits and units. Under them the reduction map from level $n$ to $m\leq n$ is
$$ (f^!_{A_n}K_n)\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m\xrightarrow{c_{n,m}(K_n)}f^!_{A_m}(K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m)\xrightarrow{f^!_{A_m}(r^K_{n,m})}f^!_{A_m}K_m,$$
where $c_{n,m}$ is the coefficient comparison of [det-sp-reduction-exceptional].

proof.text: Fix $K=K_\bullet$ and abbreviate $F_Z=R(f|_Z)_{!,\bullet}$ for opens $Z\subseteq X$. The standing schemes are Noetherian: a field has just the ideals $0,(1)$ and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applies to the structure morphisms. The statement [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian] then says that $X$ and every open in it are Noetherian and quasi-compact. By [lem-sc-standard-smooth-local-relative-dimension] every point has a standard-smooth affine neighbourhood of relative dimension $d$ over an affine open $T\subseteq Y$. The etale polynomial chart of [lem-sc-standard-smooth-etale-polynomial-chart] gives $U\to\mathbf A^d_T$; composing with $\mathbf A^d_T\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^d_Y$ remains etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Thus choose a finite cover $X=\bigcup_{i=1}^rU_i$ by such charts. Every open subset of a chart is again a chart by the same etale composition statement. If $X$ is empty, the zero pair represents the zero functor; henceforth use induction on $r\geq1$.

source.place: Local pairs and Gluing: existence of a finite coordinate cover

proof.text:
Check the domain of the current projective-line adjunction before composing it. Every scheme here (including each intermediate affine or projective space) is separated and of finite type over $k$, hence Noetherian and qcqs by Step 1's argument, and $\ell$ is invertible since $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. Each $A_n$ is finite and Noetherian. The finite-category identification proved in Step 3 below identifies every ctf level used here with the ordinary intrinsic finite-coefficient ctf category. Therefore [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] supplies an etale-origin witness for each such level. Uniform cohomological vanishing makes these towers bounded below: their cohomology is computed levelwise in the Grothendieck tower category. Thus they lie in the actual $\mathscr C^+$ domains of [det-sp-tower-p1-adjunction], whose last sentence explicitly restricts its adjunction to the uniform ctf subcategories. In particular $j_{!,\bullet}M$ is in that domain by [lem-sp-coefficient-tower-shriek-calculus](2). The same check applies at every successive affine-line projection, and the inverse images and twists remain ctf by Step 3. The witnesses are chosen separately at each level; no compatibility of witnesses as a tower is needed or asserted. Let $q:\mathbf P^1_S\to S$, $j:\mathbf A^1_S\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_S$, and $p=qj$. By [lem-sp-coefficient-tower-shriek-calculus] and [det-sp-tower-p1-adjunction], the adjunction bijections are
$$\operatorname{Hom}(Rp_{!,\bullet}M,K)=\operatorname{Hom}(Rq_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}M,K)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(j_{!,\bullet}M,q_\bullet^*K(1)[2])\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(M,p_\bullet^*K(1)[2]).$$
The base-change-compatible finite twist identification of [lem-pur-finite-kummer-level] applies with uniformizer exponent $en$ and $N=n$, because $\ell$ is a unit times $\varpi^e$. The base-change maps for roots of unity send a section $u$ to its pullback; they commute with $u\mapsto u^\ell$ because pullback preserves multiplication. After tensoring by $A_n$ these are compatible maps of the twist towers. Apply the monoidal derived pullback isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to the ringed inverse-system topoi, and use the tensor-power definition of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Their tensor associators identify the successive pulled-back twists with the sum twist as an actual tower isomorphism. This constructs the comparison before evaluating it; levelwise base change is used to check invertibility, not equality of derived tower morphisms. Compose the bijections for the $d$ successive affine-line projections and then for $e_!\dashv e^*$ on a chart $U$. This gives the local right adjoint $H_UK=e^*p_d^*K(d)[2d]$ and local representing counit $\varepsilon_U:F_UH_UK\to K$. For $d=0$ the projection part is the identity adjunction. The formula for the composite counit is $\varepsilon_{p_d}\circ Rp_{d!}(\varepsilon_e)$, so fibre summation precedes integration. Both cited statements specify finite evaluations of their adjunctions, so all these local maps are actual tower morphisms with the specified finite units and counits.

source.place: Local pairs: affine line, iteration, etale composition

proof.text: At each finite level we work in the ordinary module category over the constant ring $A_n$ of the coefficient-tower definition. Its constructibility condition in [sk-def-sfb-constructible] agrees with intrinsic finite-coefficient constructibility [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]: by [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{en}$ is finite; a finitely presented $A_n$-module is finite as a quotient of $A_n^r$, and a finite $A_n$-module has a finite presentation since the kernel of $A_n^r\twoheadrightarrow P$ is a finite set. A finite scalar matrix gives the constant sheaf of its cokernel, since [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact](2) says sheafification preserves colimits; thus the two definitions give the same local models on the same strata. Their Tor conditions quantify over exactly the same ordinary module sheaves and derived tensor product, as in [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Moreover a finite ring is Noetherian because its set of ideals is finite, and all schemes and opens used here are qcqs by Step 1 (their open intersections are quasi-compact). Hence [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] supplies etale-origin representatives and preserves each specified Tor interval whenever the current finite-level bound requires them. This does not identify completed or condensed module categories with ordinary ones: the levels already are ordinary constant-ring module sheaves. The local pair belongs to the required category. By [sk-lem-sp-tower-levels], ordinary constant-coefficient inverse image on towers is exact and computed levelwise. Inverse image preserves the finite local models and finite stratifications in [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: pull back the stratification and each displayed local presentation. It also preserves a Tor interval: [lem-sf-flat-model] supplies a bounded flat model in precisely that interval on the small pro-etale site; [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-flat-module-pullback] says every pulled-back term is flat. Exactness preserves its quasi-isomorphism to the pulled-back complex, so this is a flat model in the same interval. The finite quotient $\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$ is $\mathcal O_E/\varpi^{en}$, since $\ell$ is a unit times $\varpi^e$, so the finite-coefficient hypothesis of the flat-model lemma is satisfied. The twist is locally free of rank one by [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free], applied to the finite quotient $\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$ (a power of the uniformizer); tensoring with it preserves these bounds. Hence if the cohomological and Tor intervals of $K_n$ are $[a,b]$ and $[u,v]$, those of $H_UK_n$ are $[a-2d,b-2d]$ and $[u-2d,v-2d]$, uniformly in $n$. The definition [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers] requires exactly these levelwise conditions. An open restriction of $f$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]; it has the same pure fibre dimension $d$, because its fibres are open in the smooth pure-$d$ fibres of $f$. By [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](1), base change to any geometric point remains smooth of relative dimension $d$; thus every nonempty geometric fibre of each restriction has dimension $d$. Also $F_Z$ preserves this tower category for every such open $Z$ by [sk-lem-sp-tower-bound]; its uniform compact-support bounds are [det-sp-tower-bound-uniform], applied with these geometric-fibre bounds, the finite commutative discrete rings $A_n$, the ordinary finite-Tor categories just identified, and their etale-origin representatives. The theorem gives the common Tor interval $[u,v+2d]$ and cohomology vanishing outside it for the compact-support image.

source.place: Uniformity: local right-adjoint and compact-support bounds

proof.text:
Suppose $U,V$ cover an open $Z\subseteq X$, with pairs $(G_U,\varepsilon_U)$ and $(G_V,\varepsilon_V)$ already representing the local functors; put $W=U\cap V$. For an open inclusion $i:W\hookrightarrow U$, [lem-sp-coefficient-tower-shriek-calculus] gives $F_W=F_Ui_!$ and $i_!\dashv i^*$, with $i_!$ preserving the constructible tower category. Thus
$$\operatorname{Hom}(N,G_U|_W)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(i_!N,G_U)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(F_WN,K).$$
The associated counit is $\varepsilon_U\circ F_U(i_!i^*G_U\to G_U)$. With $i_V:W\hookrightarrow V$ the second restriction has the bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(N,G_V|_W)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(i_{V!}N,G_V)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(F_WN,K)$ and counit $\varepsilon_V\circ F_V(i_{V!}i_V^*G_V\to G_V)$. There is a unique counit-preserving isomorphism $c:G_U|_W\to G_V|_W$: apply the second representing bijection to the first counit to get $c$, and reverse the roles to get its inverse; injectivity of the two bijections makes both composites identities. This argument uses representing pairs on $W$, rather than asserting that arbitrary local derived isomorphisms glue uniquely.

By [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian], the coefficient towers on $Z$ are modules over the ring object $\mathcal O_{E,Z}/\ell^\bullet$ in the Grothendieck topos of inverse systems of pro-etale sheaves. The constant inverse systems of the subterminal sheaves $U,V,W$ are open subtopoi with $U\cup V=Z$. For each open $D=U,V,W$, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization](1) identifies $D_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with $Z_{\mathrm{proét}}/D$, and (2) identifies the restricted constant ring $A_n$ with its constant ring on $D$. These identifications preserve the constant-section quotient maps $A_n\to A_m$. Applying them levelwise identifies the slice module category with the coefficient-tower category on $D$: its objects and arrows are the restricted module sheaves and semilinear transitions. Apply [lem-sp-ringed-topos-binary-descent](1) in this ringed topos to $G_U,G_V,c$. It gives an actual object $G\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(Z,\mathcal O_E))$ with the prescribed restrictions. Concretely it is the fibre, not the unshifted cone, of
$$Rj_{U*}G_U\oplus Rj_{V*}G_V\longrightarrow Rj_{W*}(G_V|_W).$$
The intermediate derived direct images need not be constructible; the glued object is. Exact restriction and evaluation show its cohomology vanishes outside the common local interval. Each cohomology sheaf is constructible by [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: combine the finitely many local stratifications, refining their finitely many intersections and complements to a finite locally closed stratification of the Noetherian scheme. The same restriction test applied to $G_n\otimes^L N$ gives its common Tor interval. A sheaf vanishing on both members is zero by the sheaf condition. Consequently $G$ belongs to the category of [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers].

source.place: Gluing and Uniformity: construct the global object correctly

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sp-ringed-topos-binary-descent](2) to $G$ and then the exact compact-support functor $F_Z$ of [lem-sp-coefficient-tower-shriek-calculus]. The result is the triangle
$$F_W(G|_W)\to F_U(G|_U)\oplus F_V(G|_V)\to F_ZG\longrightarrow.$$
Under the selected restriction isomorphisms, the map $(\varepsilon_U,\varepsilon_V)$ to $K$ kills the first arrow: its two components are the same overlap counit by the definition of $c$ in Step 4, and the first arrow has signs $(1,-1)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact](i) it factors through a map $\varepsilon:F_ZG\to K$. This is the needed global counit. Only existence of this lift has been used.

source.place: Gluing: lift the compatible local counits

proof.text: For arbitrary $M$ in the constructible tower category, apply the two contravariant functors $\operatorname{Hom}(-,G)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(F_Z(-),K)$ to the open-cover triangle of Step 6 with $M$ in place of $G$. The arrows $\theta_N:a\mapsto\varepsilon F_Z(a)$ form a morphism of these exact Hom sequences: for each triangle arrow $t:N\to N'$ one has $\varepsilon F_Z(a\circ t)=\varepsilon F_Z(a)\circ F_Z(t)$, including the shifted boundary arrow. Exactness at all positions follows by rotations and shifts from [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact]. By [lem-sp-coefficient-tower-shriek-calculus] and the local adjunctions, $\theta$ is a bijection on all shifts of $j_{U!}(M|_U)$, $j_{V!}(M|_V)$ and $j_{W!}(M|_W)$. Indeed transposing $a:j_{U!}N\to G$ gives $a_U:N\to G_U$, and $\theta(a)=\varepsilon_UF_U(a_U)$ by the restriction equation of Step 6. For $D=U,V,W$, let $j_D:D\hookrightarrow Z$ and let $\varepsilon_D$ be the restricted representing counit. For every integer $t$, the open adjunction sends $a:j_{D!}(N[t])\to G$ to $a_D:N[t]\to G|_D$, and the restriction equation gives $\theta(a)=\varepsilon_DF_D(a_D)$. Thus each shifted vertical map is exactly the corresponding local representing bijection. In the five-term segment of the two exact sequences with $\theta_M$ in the centre, the other four vertical arrows are bijective. To see the central bijectivity directly, lift the image of a bottom central element to the top term on its right; its next image is zero by the rightmost injection, so exactness lifts it to the top centre, and the residual bottom element comes from the left and can be lifted using the left surjection. For injectivity a central kernel element has zero right image, hence comes from the top left; its bottom left image lies in the image of the preceding bottom term, which lifts by the leftmost surjection, leaving zero by the adjacent left injection. Thus $\theta_M$ is a bijection, natural in $M$. This proves representability of $(G,\varepsilon)$.

Use induction on the finite cover in Step 1. For a single chart the pair is Step 2. Given the pair on $Z=U_1\cup\cdots\cup U_{r-1}$, use $U=Z$, $V=U_r$ in Steps 4–7. The intersection is an open of the chart $U_r$, so its chart pair is available, and Step 4 also identifies the restriction of the pair from $Z$ with it. This constructs the pair on $X$. For an additional coordinate chart $j:D\hookrightarrow X$, open adjunction and $F_Xj_!=F_D$ give $\operatorname{Hom}(N,G|_D)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(j_!N,G)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(F_DN,K)$, with counit $\varepsilon F_X(j_!j^*G\to G)$. The unique counit-preserving comparison of representing pairs therefore identifies $G|_D$ with the chart pair in Step 2. This proves clause 1 for every chart, not just the chosen atlas.

source.place: Gluing: finite induction and arbitrary charts

proof.text: If $(G,\varepsilon)$ and $(G',\varepsilon')$ represent the same functor, take $M=G$ in the second bijection to obtain the unique $a:G\to G'$ with $\varepsilon'F(a)=\varepsilon$. Reversing the roles gives $b:G'\to G$; injectivity gives $ba=1$ and $ab=1$. For $u:K\to L$, define $G(u)$ as the unique map with $\varepsilon_LF(G(u))=u\varepsilon_K$. Applying this equation twice proves preservation of identities and composition. It also proves naturality in $K$ of the representing bijections. Set $\eta_M$ equal to the transpose of $1_{FM}$. The transpose equations give $\varepsilon_{FM}F(\eta_M)=1_{FM}$ and, by injectivity, $G(\varepsilon_K)\eta_{GK}=1_{GK}$. These are the two adjunction identities and prove clause 2 without requiring a functorial choice of cones.

source.place: Uniqueness and functoriality: explicit inverse maps and adjunction

proof.text:
Evaluation at $n$ is exact by [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian] and therefore induces a triangulated functor by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. For compact support, [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](1) applies because every tower evaluated here is bounded below by its uniform cohomological bound; it gives exactly the finite operation for the chosen compactification. Open extension and its finite adjunction maps are supplied by [lem-sp-coefficient-tower-shriek-calculus](2). No projection formula from [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](2)(a), whose field hypothesis is more restrictive, is invoked. By [det-sp-tower-p1-adjunction], the evaluated chart adjunction of Step 2 has the finite unit and counit. Prove finite representability by induction on the actual chart cover used in Step 8. The empty case is the zero category, and the single-chart case is the finite chart adjunction. Its finite test objects and all their open extensions are ordinary ctf objects over finite Noetherian $A_n$ on qcqs schemes; [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] gives their etale-origin representatives by the same finite-category check as Step 3. Thus the restricted projective-line adjunction used in Step 2 applies, and its evaluation gives the required finite counit even with the current etale-origin domain. For the binary induction step $Z=U\cup V$, put $W=U\cap V$ and let $G_{Z,n},\varepsilon_{Z,n}$ be the evaluated constructed pair. Its restrictions to $U,V,W$ have the finite representing counits by induction, the finite chart case for the overlap, and the evaluated restriction equation of Step 6. Take an arbitrary finite ctf object $M$ on $Z$, without assuming that it lifts to a tower. By [lem-sp-ringed-topos-binary-descent](2), put $A=j_{W!}(M|_W)$, $B=j_{U!}(M|_U)\oplus j_{V!}(M|_V)$ in the triangle $A\to B\to M\to A[1]$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact] and its rotated shifts gives the exact segment
$$\operatorname{Hom}(B[1],G_{Z,n})\to\operatorname{Hom}(A[1],G_{Z,n})\to\operatorname{Hom}(M,G_{Z,n})\to\operatorname{Hom}(B,G_{Z,n})\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,G_{Z,n}),$$
and the segment with terms $\operatorname{Hom}(F_{Z,n}(-),K_n)$. The vertical map at $N$ is $a\mapsto\varepsilon_{Z,n}F_{Z,n}(a)$; it commutes with each arrow $t$ because $\varepsilon_{Z,n}F_{Z,n}(a\circ t)=\varepsilon_{Z,n}F_{Z,n}(a)F_{Z,n}(t)$, also for the boundary $M\to A[1]$. Open adjunction identifies the four outer vertical maps with the finite local representing bijections, including shifted ones. For surjectivity at the centre, lift the image in the fourth bottom term through the fourth vertical bijection; its image in the fifth top term vanishes, so exactness lifts it to the top centre. The residual bottom central element comes from the second bottom term and lifts through its bijection. For injectivity, a central kernel element comes from the second top term; its image below comes from the first bottom term, which lifts through the first bijection. Subtract that first top image; injectivity at the second term makes the remainder zero. Hence the central map is bijective. This completes induction and proves finite representability for every finite test object. The current statement of [det-sp-reduction-exceptional] names the constructible adjunction on the ordinary constant-ring categories in the standing scheme setting, with the fixed coefficient-independent compactification. These are exactly our finite categories and chosen compactification; $f$ has pure relative dimension $d\geq0$, and $A_n$ is finite and annihilated by $\ell^n$. Its representing finite adjoint $f^!_{A_n}$ therefore has a unique counit-preserving comparison with $G_n$. Evaluating $\varepsilon_LF(G(u))=u\varepsilon_K$ identifies the action on every tower morphism with the action of the finite adjoint. Finally $\varepsilon_{FM}F(\eta_M)=1$ evaluates to the finite transpose equation for $1_{F_nM_n}$, so injectivity of the finite bijection identifies the units. This proves the first part of clause 3.

source.place: Levels: finite representability and units, without exchanging evaluation and Hom

proof.text:
Use the chosen compactification $f=\bar f\circ j$ supplied by [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], the same compactification used in [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](1), whose bounded-below hypothesis follows from the uniform cohomological bounds of $G$ and $K$. To apply [det-sp-reduction-direct-image], take its coefficient map to be $A=A_n\to B=A_m$, its object $M=G_n$, and its compactification to be this $j,\bar f$. Indeed $f$ is separated and of finite type; if $\ell=u\varpi_E^e$ with $u$ a unit, then $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{en}$ and $A_m=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{em}$ are finite commutative rings by [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], killed by $\ell^n$ and $\ell^m$. The quotient map exists since $m\leq n$, and $G_n\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proét}},A_n)$ by Steps 3, 5 and 10. For [det-sp-reduction-exceptional] this quotient is unital, $N=\ell^n$ is a common annihilator of $A_n,A_m$, and the same coefficient-independent compactification and ordinary constant-ring ctf categories are used. The finite identifications from Step 10 preserve the specified counits, so its defining transpose identity uses precisely the $\varepsilon_n$, $\varepsilon_m$ and canonical $b_f$ below; no chartwise detection of equality is needed. Thus the cited statement gives the isomorphism
$$b_f(G_n):(R\bar f_*j_!G_n)\otimes^L_{A_{n,Y}}A_{m,Y}\xrightarrow{\sim}R\bar f_*j_!\bigl(G_n\otimes^L_{A_{n,X}}A_{m,X}\bigr).$$
Here the proper comparison is the $A_m$-linear adjoint transpose of the $A_n$-counit after extension of scalars, followed by the canonical open-extension tensor comparison, exactly as specified by the current direct-image statement. Step 3 identifies its intrinsic ordinary finite-coefficient ctf category with the actual tower levels. This is exactly the finite coefficient comparison in [lem-sp-coefficient-tower-shriek-calculus](3); no change of compactification or choice of a different level isomorphism is being made. Let $r_G:(G_n)_{A_m}\to G_m$ and $r_K:(K_n)_{A_m}\to K_m$ be the natural reduction maps of [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian], and use the counit-preserving finite identifications of Step 10. Naturality of reduction for the actual tower map $\varepsilon:FG\to K$, together with calculus (3), gives
$$\varepsilon_m F_{f,m}(r_G)b_f(G_n)=r_K(\varepsilon_n)_{A_m},$$
hence
$$\varepsilon_m F_{f,m}(r_G)=r_K(\varepsilon_n)_{A_m}b_f(G_n)^{-1}.$$
The common source is $F_{f,m}((G_n)_{A_m})$ and the common target is $K_m$. Naturality of the finite counit and the defining transpose equation of [det-sp-reduction-exceptional], applied with the same coefficient map $A_n\to A_m$ and $K_n\in\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},A_n)$, give
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon_m F_{f,m}\bigl(f^!_{A_m}(r_K)c_{n,m}(K_n)\bigr)
&=r_K\varepsilon_{m,(K_n)_{A_m}}F_{f,m}(c_{n,m}(K_n))\\
&=r_K(\varepsilon_n)_{A_m}b_f(G_n)^{-1}.
\end{aligned}$$
The inverse of $b_f(G_n)$ exists by the quoted direct-image statement, which imposes no flatness or finite projective dimension hypothesis on $A_m$ over $A_n$. Injectivity of the finite adjunction bijection with test object $(G_n)_{A_m}$ therefore gives $r_G=f^!_{A_m}(r_K)c_{n,m}(K_n)$. This proves the reduction formula for arbitrary, possibly nonnormalized towers. When $n=m$ both reductions and their canonical comparisons are identities; for $n\geq m\geq r$, the composition clause of the direct-image comparison and the reduction-map composition law identify both iterated transposes with that for $A_n\to A_r$. The argument uses equality of global transposes, rather than testing equality of derived morphisms only after local restriction.
